newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB set to decide on satellite decoder-FT.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB set to decide on satellite decoder-FT.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting, the satellite television arm of News International Plc is set to make a decision on whether to order one million decoder boxes for its digital satellite TV service within a few days, the Financial Times reported.

The newspaper said that if the decision is taken, orders worth more than 200 million pounds could be placed with a shortlist of six consumer electronics groups including Pace Micro Technology Plc, Amstrad, Sony Panasonic and Nokia.
Commenting on the report, a spokesman for BSkyB said: "There is nothing I can say at this time of night."

Earlier this month, papers reported that the manufacturers of the decoder boxes needed to receive digital channels had warned BSkyB that it must order the boxes at this time to guarantee the sets will be ready on time for next year's launch.

Digital technology is set to revolutionise TV programming with hundreds of channels available plus other services like pay per view and home shopping but consumer groups and other broadcasters have warned that unless BSkyB opens its system to others, there might be a need for more than one decoder in each home and that the Murdoch company will come to dominate the market.
